after.level_assignment_reason: The measured endpoint is nuclear γH2AX foci, a direct marker of DNA double-strand damage, in human bronchial epithelial cells after B[ghi]p exposure. This is a DNA lesion/damage assay, which belongs in L4, not the epigenetic/intercellular growth restraint family (L6). The positive result and ROS-independence are relevant mechanistic evidence for genotoxicity, not a tumor outcome or epigenetic endpoint.

Cyclophosphamide 80 mg/kg (positive control) gave 24h MNPCE% F 14.6*, M 15.7*. PCE/(PCE+NCE) ratios remained ~50-54%.

It should not remain in a near-direct carcinogenicity level.

after.reviewed_record_json: {"paragraph_idx":0,"support_text":"Metabolism of VP-16-213 (etoposide, VP-16) by mouse liver microsomes to reactive intermediates and subsequent covalent binding to microsomal proteins was studied. The metabolism involved O-demethylation of VP-16 resulting in formation of a 3',4'-dihydroxy derivative (DHVP-16), identified by HPLC and mass spectrometry. after.level_assignment_reason: The card primarily measures receptor-mediated TEB density and epithelial-layer growth, which alone fits L7. However, the support text and interpretation explicitly state that parathion-containing treatments increased epithelial layers followed by mammary carcinomas, an agent-attributed tumor outcome. This mixed passage therefore belongs in L2 as an overall tumor assertion, not only L7 mechanistic growth.

after.reviewed_record_json: {"paragraph_idx":31,"support_text":"We used 0.05 μM isopsoralen instead of 10 μg/ml insulin to induce chondrogenic differentiation of ATDC5 cells. before.support_text: Using OB-6 osteoblastic cells, angelicin was able to attenuate H2O2-induced damage, increasing cell viability and decreasing the apoptotic rate with suppression of ROS generation. Angelicin also successfully induced osteogenic differentiation via the Wnt/β-catenin pathway even under oxidative stress. An increase in calcium accumulation, and in osteogenic differentiation markers (OCN and Runx2) and Wnt/β-catenin pathway markers (β-catenin and tankyrase) was reported when angelicin was co-treated with H2O2 in OB-6 osteoblastic cells.

after.qualifying_conditions: Angelicin is isopsoralen; modifier of H2O2 oxidative challenge. Same-study cell viability/apoptosis retained in L3. Normal calcium deposition, Runx2/OCN and osteogenic differentiation are separated from this redox endpoint.
after.support_text: In H2O2-challenged OB-6 cells, isopsoralen (angelicin) reduced ROS production and ameliorated the reduction in mitochondrial respiratory-chain complex I activity. These are redox/mitochondrial measurements; the study separately measured cell viability, apoptosis and osteogenic differentiation.

before.support_text: DC did not exhibit cytotoxicity in RAW 264.7 cells (Figure 1A) or in RANKL-induced osteoclasts (Figure 1B). RANKL-treated cells differentiated into red giant multinucleated cells by TRAP staining, and DC inhibited this differentiation, especially 200 μg/mL of DC, which resulted in a cell size and color similar to RANKL(−). Counting the number of differentiated cells, RANKL induced a significant increase in the number of osteoclasts, and DC inhibited this increase in a concentration-dependent manner. DC also significantly inhibited RANKL-induced TRAP activity in the culture medium in a concentration-dependent manner, and inhibited the mRNA expression of TRAP (Acp5).

before.support_text: Osteoclasts are formed by the differentiation, fusion, and maturation of precursor cells. RAW 264.7 cells were stimulated with RANKL and treated with DC (demethylasterriquinone) for 0–2, 2–4, and 4–6 days. DC reduced the size and number of osteoclasts and attenuated their red color in all time periods, with the strongest inhibitory effect on osteoclast differentiation at the beginning of differentiation (days 0–2). Consistent with the staining, TRAP activity in the culture medium showed DC was most effective at the early stage of differentiation.

before.support_text: Rats received 250 mg/kg/day of GOH for four weeks after traumatic spinal cord injury introduced by a surgical procedure [234]. The observed regeneration at the injury site by the GOH treatment was mediated through modulation of NF-κB and p38 MAPK, and the inflammatory response, oxidative stress, and caspase-9 and -3 activities were significantly suppressed. This is a secondary report cited by the review (PMID 30096653).

after.canonical_measurement_text: Low-to-moderate GGOH concentrations increased metabolic viability; high GGOH reduced viability and could exacerbate zoledronate-associated cell death

after.qualifying_conditions: Fliefel2019, primary PMID30728841. Separate GGOH-alone and zoledronate combination conditions. Response is dose-dependent; WST-1 and live/dead microscopy are separate readouts and need not agree at borderline concentrations. TRAP differentiation is not used as a cancer-growth endpoint.
after.support_text: Fliefel et al. measured human osteoclast metabolic viability by WST-1 and evaluated live/dead staining after GGOH exposure, alone or with zoledronate. Lower GGOH concentrations could rescue viability, whereas the highest tested concentration reduced viability and enhanced cell death. Normal osteoclast TRAP differentiation was a separate measurement.
after.level_assignment_reason: Retain verified dose-dependent cell survival/death in L3 while separating normal osteoclast differentiation. Do not equate live/dead staining with apoptosis-specific mechanism.
